name: Projected Terminal Text Viewer
description: Provides a bounded, keyboard-first immutable read view for shell-marked command output or the complete retained scrollback owned by one projected terminal client.

states: Inspect immutable plain-text output, the retained-history notice, literal search highlights, match navigation, copy, close, and terminal-focus restoration.
Use Control+Shift+G to open from terminal focus, Command+F or Control+F to return to the query, Enter and Shift+Enter to cycle, and Escape to close.
Inspect the complete immutable retained-history document and its initial visible-top anchor.
Use Control+Shift+H to open from terminal focus, Command+F or Control+F to focus search, Enter and Shift+Enter to cycle, and Escape to close.
Inspect the localized no-output result with the close action focused and search and copy controls absent.
Inspect the bounded source-limit result without exposing partial command output.

useWhen: One projected terminal client must inspect, search, or copy either the most recent output delimited by retained shell markers or its complete retained primary-screen history.
avoidWhen: The task needs arbitrary external pagers, ANSI re-rendering, history beyond Terminal Host retention, or output from more than one terminal.
invariants: The viewer opens only from an exact generation-and-revision extraction and never renders partial content after cancellation, staleness, eviction, or the source limit.
The prepared plain-text document remains immutable while open; search state never triggers another terminal-history read.
Literal case-insensitive search is bounded to 1,024 query characters and 1,000 non-overlapping matches.
Copy executes the source-specific terminal.output.copy or terminal.history.copy Action and never writes the clipboard directly from the presentational component.
The modal focus cycle remains inside the viewer, terminal shortcuts fall through while it owns focus, and close restores terminal focus.
No-output, no-scrollback, missing-shell-integration, alternate-screen, stale, source-limit, and unavailable outcomes remain localized and disclose no partial text.
